# Monte Carlo evaluation

<!-- Generated by sifted_montecarlo (eval/sifted_montecarlo.cpp) via `python3 -m sifted_sim.montecarlo report`. Do not edit by hand. -->

The scorecard ([evaluation.md](evaluation.md)) scores one sensor-noise realisation per scenario. Its seeds vary only the network, so a zero there may be the luck of one draw. This page scores many independent realisations of every multi-target scenario and a clutter and detection-probability sweep. Each metric is reported as a mean over runs with a 95% interval, alongside how many runs had any identity break at all. The comparison with an external baseline tracker is [evaluation-baseline.md](evaluation-baseline.md).

## What was run

```bash
cmake --preset release && cmake --build --preset release
PYTHONPATH=sim python3 -m sifted_sim.montecarlo report
```

which runs `sifted_montecarlo --manifest MANIFEST` on the generated manifest. Base seed 20261119, 1500 generated runs. Each run's sensor seeds derive from (base seed, scenario, run index) through SplitMix64 (`sim/sifted_sim/montecarlo.py`), the same in every condition. Scenarios: `close_pass`, `crossing_pair`, `demo`, `enter_leave`, `formation_split` (definitions in `sim/sifted_sim/scenarios.py`).

## Findings

- **Accuracy over fresh noise.** Over 500 independent realisations, sifted's mean RMSE is 10.02 [9.44, 10.66] m. The worst target RMSE of a run has median 9.10 m, but the worst single run reaches 60.13 m: one noise draw per scenario cannot show that tail.
- **Identity breaks.** 9.2 [7.0, 12.1]% of runs break identity at least once (0.212 [0.154, 0.274] ID switches per run). By scenario: `formation_split` 46.0 [36.6, 55.7]% of runs (1.06 [0.82, 1.30] per run); `close_pass` 0.0 [0.0, 3.7]% of runs (0 [0, 0.04] per run); `crossing_pair` 0.0 [0.0, 3.7]% of runs (0 [0, 0.04] per run); `demo` 0.0 [0.0, 3.7]% of runs (0 [0, 0.04] per run); `enter_leave` 0.0 [0.0, 3.7]% of runs (0 [0, 0.04] per run). Breaks concentrate where targets fly closer than a few measurement sigmas for many scans in a row. Their gates then overlap, and on a scan whose noise makes the swapped pairing cheaper, even the global (Hungarian) assignment swaps the tracks. Once swapped, each track follows the other target, and the scorer counts the switch and the larger error. The average hides how uneven this is: most runs have none, a few have several.
- **Network impairment.** Through the pipeline under moderate impairment, the same runs score 2.24 [1.77, 2.73] m higher mean RMSE and 0.078 [0.020, 0.136] more ID switches per run than the direct feed (paired).
- **Clutter, Pd 0.7.** False tracks per run: 0.03 [0.00, 0.07] at 0.5, 0.85 [0.67, 1.04] at 5, 26.15 [24.09, 28.36] at 20, 152.06 [143.39, 160.61] at 50, 443.37 [422.72, 464.48] at 100 clutter points per scan. From 5 to 100 points per scan (x20 the clutter) they grow x522, faster than the clutter itself. Mean RMSE on the true targets stays between 11.64 and 12.91 m. The track cap was never reached (TrackLimit 0).
- **Clutter, Pd 0.9.** False tracks per run: 0.03 [0.00, 0.07] at 0.5, 0.85 [0.67, 1.04] at 5, 26.14 [24.18, 28.23] at 20, 152.09 [143.99, 160.92] at 50, 442.65 [422.10, 462.20] at 100 clutter points per scan. From 5 to 100 points per scan (x20 the clutter) they grow x521, faster than the clutter itself. Mean RMSE on the true targets stays between 9.34 and 11.72 m. The track cap was never reached (TrackLimit 0).
- **Why false tracks grow with clutter.** Any range-bearing detection that no established track takes starts a tentative track, and a tentative track is confirmed after 3 hits in its chi-square gate with no gap over 3 s. Clutter is uniform over the coverage disc, so both the number of clutter-born tentative tracks and the chance that clutter falls in their gates on the next scans rise with clutter density, and the confirmations multiply. GNN still gives the true detection to the true target's track, which is why accuracy on real targets barely moves. The GOSPA decomposition shows the cost: under heavy clutter almost all of GOSPA is false tracks. This is the confirmation logic's limit (3-of-3 at 1 Hz), not a failure of association. The baseline comparison isolates the motion model's part in it.

## Targets never tracked

No target was left untracked in any run: every target that should have been tracked has an RMSE in every run.

## Method and metric definitions

- **Unit of analysis: the run.** Every interval is computed from one value per run (a run's RMSE, ID-switch count, GOSPA, ...), never from time samples within a run, which are strongly correlated.
- **Point estimates and intervals.** Mean over runs with a 95% seeded percentile bootstrap interval (2000 resamples, base seed 1; `eval/sifted/eval/stats.hpp`). Counts (ID switches, false tracks) are skewed, and the bootstrap makes no normality assumption. With no event in n runs it shows `0 [0, u]`: u = -ln(0.025)/n = 3.69/n is the exact Poisson 95% upper bound on the mean per run. Fractions of runs ("runs with an ID switch") use the Wilson score interval.
- **Paired comparisons** use common random numbers: run r of a scenario has the same sensor noise, detections and clutter in every condition and for every tracker, so the difference is taken run by run and the interval is the bootstrap of the mean difference. "No detectable difference" means the interval contains 0.
- **Scoring** is the scorecard's own (`eval/sifted/eval/scenario.hpp`, [evaluation.md](evaluation.md)): CLEAR-MOT style matching within 100 m. RMSE per target over covered, matched instants at least 10 s after the target enters coverage; a run's mean RMSE averages its tracked targets and its worst RMSE is its largest. Missed %: covered target-instants at least 5 s after entering coverage with no matched track. ID switch: a target matched to a different track than the last time it was matched. False track: a reported track matched to a target in fewer than half of the instants it was reported.
- **GOSPA** (alpha = 2; Rahmathullah, García-Fernández and Svensson, FUSION 2017, arXiv:1601.05585; `eval/sifted/eval/gospa.hpp`) with **c = 100 m, p = 2**, per truth instant from 5 s after the first, between the targets counted for "missed" and the reported (confirmed and coasting) tracks. A track matched to a target that is present but out of coverage or still in its burn-in is left out of both sets. c equals the matching distance, so a GOSPA miss or false track is what the CLEAR-MOT matcher would call one (sized at about 5x the filtered radar error at the 8 km edge of coverage and below the closest lane spacing, 120 m). p = 2 weighs localisation errors as RMSE does. A run's GOSPA is (mean over instants of d^p)^(1/p), the RMS GOSPA for p = 2. The decomposition splits the mean d^p into localisation (assigned pairs), missed targets and false tracks (c^p/2 each), exactly additive.
- **Never tracked**: target-runs where the target was covered past the RMSE burn-in but never matched. Their RMSE is undefined. They are counted here, not dropped silently, and the RMSE columns average only the runs and targets that have one.
- **TrackLimit**: measurements that could not start a track because the engine was at `max_tracks` (1024), summed over runs (runs with any). Not available (n/a) for external trackers.
- **Determinism.** The same binary on the same architecture, given the same manifest (scenario code and base seed), writes the same bytes. Different compilers or maths libraries may change the last bits of the simulated noise (Python `sin`/`cos`) or of the filters, and so individual runs. The intervals are meant to absorb exactly that kind of variation.
